# Runbook: Celery broker (ElastiCache Redis) failover

Last reviewed: 2026-11-05 (after INC-0412)

finalize_invoice is acks_late: after a broker failover, in-flight tasks are redelivered. Since #1497 (INV-2240) redelivery is safe: side effects are deduplicated on (invoice_id, kind, target).

1. Confirm the failover in the ElastiCache console (events tab) and in #inc channel.
2. Watch the redelivery rate on the billing-worker dashboard; a spike that decays within ~30 minutes is expected.
3. Restart workers only if they're not consuming: `ecs update-service --force-new-deployment` for billing-worker.
4. Never purge the queue: `celery purge` deletes legitimate work (finalizations, reminders) that cannot be recovered.
5. Schedule ElastiCache service updates yourself, off-peak (before 07:00 CT), never leave them to auto-apply.
6. Post in #incidents when the redelivery rate is back to baseline.

# INC-0412 postmortem (draft, blameless). SEV-2, Wednesday 2026-11-04

Summary: an auto-applied ElastiCache service update failed over the Celery broker at 10:04 CT. finalize_invoice (acks_late) tasks were redelivered; side effects weren't deduplicated (INV-2240), so 41 invoices for 9 tenants sent duplicate invoice emails (41) and webhooks (66). Resolved 16:50 after #1497.

Timeline (CT): 10/30 handoff notes the pending update and INV-2240. 11/2 10:00 AWS notice: auto-apply 11/4 10:00-11:00. 11/3 13:45 #1497 opened. 11/4 10:04 failover; 10:05 page; 10:12 SEV-2, Marcus IC; 10:20 queue purge proposed per stale runbook, stopped; 10:31 redeliveries end; 11:15 impact posted; 11:30 hotfix #1496 proposed, not merged (race, locking index); 12:30 #1497 approved as emergency change; 14:52 migration 0042 (107 duplicate rows removed, concurrent unique index); 16:50 resolved.

Impact: 41 duplicate emails, 66 duplicate webhooks (8 tenants with webhooks), downstream duplicate invoices at 2+ tenants' accounting systems. No data loss.

What went wrong: we let the maintenance auto-apply in peak hours; a known idempotency gap (INV-2240) sat as low priority since August; the runbook predated acks_late.
What went right: purge was stopped; the proper fix was already in review; impact numbers were exact within an hour.

Actions: (1) schedule service updates ourselves off-peak (owner Ben, 11/13); (2) runbook rewritten (done 11/5); (3) alert on redelivery spikes (Marcus, 11/20); (4) audit other acks_late tasks for idempotency (Jordan, 12/4); (5) customer-facing summary via CS (Marcus).
